label: nyiso 33 ct-tempfloor [keeper]
definition: NEW KEEPER (supersedes nyiso-32 steam-markup). Adds a temperature-keyed DOWNSTATE CT_PEAKER local-reliability floor (--nyiso-ct-reliability-floor) on top of the nyiso-32 steam-markup keeper -- the CAISO local-RA CT floor ported to NYISO's cable-constrained downstate load pockets (NYC zone J, Long Island zone K, Lower Hudson). On hot afternoons the downstate cooling load climbs and the UPNY-SENY / LI-cable import limits bind, so fast-start GTs are held online for local capacity-area reliability; an energy-only LP imports cheap upstate/NYC CC instead and under-runs CT_PEAKER. Floor = clip(base + slope*(TMAX-25), base, cap) x available downstate-CT capacity over HB14-21, with slope=0.053/degC, cap=0.68, base=0.13 -- ALL regressed a priori from the measured downstate CAMPD CT_PEAKER evening CF vs NYC daily max temperature (NOAA GHCN), pooled 2023-2025 (scripts/derive_nyiso_ct_reliability_floor.py; archived data/raw/nyiso-weather/). A physical heat->commitment rule, forward-reproducible (a forecast year pins a weather year, hence a TMAX series), NOT a CEMS pin and NOT residual-tuned (CT_PEAKER lands UNDER actual, so not over-forced). Result -- the HARD C1 fuel-mix improves decisively: CT_PEAKER (the open frontier on EVERY prior NYISO keeper, and confirmed non-closable via a grounded reserve REQUIREMENT by nyiso-29/31) 2023 -1.73 -> -0.85 TWh and 2024 -1.92 -> -0.85 TWh, FAIL -> PASS both scored years; the complementary CC_REGULAR over-run drops 2023 +0.99 -> +0.63 (PASS) and 2024 +1.74 -> +1.25 (FAIL -> PASS). 2023 now has every gas class in C1 tolerance. dispatch_corr stays PASS (gas r=0.91/0.85/0.80). TRADEOFF (kept per rule #1): C3a mean LMP regresses ~1.3pp (2023 -10.5 -> -11.7%, 2024 -11.2 -> -12.7%, 2025 -7.3 -> -8.6%) because the floor is a min-gen (must-run) representation -- it recovers the local-RA ENERGY but adds inframarginal supply rather than letting the peakers SET a scarcity price; the price side (C3a/C3c) remains the ledgered reserve-scarcity frontier (an ORDC/reserve-scarcity demand curve, non-closable with grounded inputs per nyiso-29/31). Remaining C1 miss: 2024 ST_GAS -3.77 TWh (the floor pulls some evening energy from downstate steam too). Most structurally faithful NYISO config to date: it adds a real, measured, forward-reproducible local-reliability mechanism that closes the largest C1 miss -- the rule-#1 'right market structure' step the reserve-requirement attempts could not take. Governance C6 PASS; determination NOT-YET (2024 ST_GAS C1 + price_shape/price_tail reserve-scarcity gap). Reproduce: nyiso-32 keeper flags + --nyiso-ct-reliability-floor (now the live default for NYISO).
